stated: Reform UK will scrap thousands of laws, including employment laws, that they claim hold back British business and damage productivity, to make it easier to hire and fire staff.

source.quote: Slash Red Tape to Boost Industry and Exports Scrap thousands of laws that hold back British business and damage productivity, including employment laws. We must make it easier to hire and fire so that businesses can grow.

bearing_set.reason: Scrapping employment laws to make it easier to hire and fire directly affects job security, employment rights, and working conditions — core O4 indicators — for the broad workforce.
The policy's explicit stated aim is to raise productivity and reduce regulatory drag on business investment and dynamism — a direct claim on aggregate living standards and economic opportunity.
Repealing thousands of regulatory mandates and obligations on businesses is a concrete reduction in state coercion, which falls squarely within O10's 'freedom from mandates/licensing' scope.

Weakening employment protections shifts bargaining power from workers to employers; the empirical literature links weaker labour-law regimes to wider wage inequality, directly moving the rich-poor gap indicator.

membership_note: Four outcomes clear the non-negligible bar: O4 (job quality/security), O13 (aggregate prosperity), O10 (deregulation as reduction in state coercion), and O14 (distributional shift in bargaining power and wages). O9 is potentially in scope if anti-discrimination employment law is among the repeals, but the policy is too vague to confirm that mechanism — left out pending specificity.
